+    let exit_container = &exits[0].2["container"];
+    let removed = exit_container["removed"] == true && exit_container["residue"].is_null();
+    let residue = exit_container["residue"].as_str();
+    let one_residue = exit_container["removed"] == false
+        && residue.is_some_and(|residue| {
+            matches!(
+                residue,
+                "kill_failed"
+                    | "termination_unconfirmed"
+                    | "remove_failed"
+                    | "remove_timeout"
+                    | "exists_failed"
+                    | "still_exists"
+                    | "volume_cleanup_unconfirmed"
+                    | "runtime_client_unconfirmed"
+            )
+        });
+    assert!(
+        removed || one_residue,
+        "container must be removed or have one typed residue: {exit_container}"
+    );
+    if removed {
+        let exists_cid = cid.clone();
+        let exists = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
+            std::process::Command::new("timeout")
+                .args(["8s", &runtime, "container", "exists", &exists_cid])
+                .status()
+                .expect("check owned CID removal")
+        })
+        .await
+        .expect("exists task");
+        assert_eq!(
+            exists.code(),
+            Some(1),
+            "exit-row CID absence requires container exists exit code 1"
+        );
+    } else {
+        supervisor.report_unresolved_containers();
+    }
+    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir);
+}
+
+fn cid_from_lifecycle(path: &Path) -> Option<String> {
+    for line in std::fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?.lines() {
+        let entry: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(line).ok()?;
+        if entry["lifecycle_event"] == "SandboxApplied" {
+            let bytes = entry["payload"].as_array()?;
+            let payload = bytes
+                .iter()
+                .map(|byte| byte.as_u64().and_then(|n| u8::try_from(n).ok()))
+                .collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
+            return serde_json::from_slice::<serde_json::Value>(&payload).ok()?["container_id"]
+                .as_str()
+                .map(str::to_owned);
+        }
+    }
+    None
+}
+async fn wait_for(budget: Duration, mut predicate: impl FnMut() -> bool) -> bool {
+    let deadline = Instant::now() + budget;
+    while Instant::now() < deadline {
+        if predicate() {
+            return true;
+        }
+        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)).await;
+    }
+    predicate()
+}

+/// A PID observed once. Never a liveness claim and never a kill target.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]

+/// The payload's own exit, as far as the evidence proves it.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum PayloadExit {
+    Unknown,
+    Exited(u8),
+    Signaled(u8),
+}
+
+impl PayloadExit {
+    /// Decode a raw wait status; `None` unless it is terminal
+    /// (`WIFEXITED`/`WIFSIGNALED`).
+    pub fn from_wait_status(raw: i32) -> Option<Self> {
+        match raw & 0x7f {
+            0 => Some(Self::Exited(((raw >> 8) & 0xff) as u8)),
+            0x7f => None,
+            signal => Some(Self::Signaled(signal as u8)),
+        }
+    }
+
+    pub fn describe(&self) -> String {
+        match self {
+            Self::Unknown => "unknown".into(),
+            Self::Exited(code) => format!("exited(code={code})"),
+            Self::Signaled(signal) => format!("signaled(sig={signal})"),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
+pub enum PayloadExitSource {
+    Pidfd,
+    Runtime,
+    None,
+}

+/// Why no terminal runtime observation exists. Bounded and non-secret.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum TerminalUnavailable {
+    InspectFailed,
+    InspectTimedOut,
+    MalformedState,
+    NonTerminal,
+    DeadlineExpired,
+}
+
+impl TerminalUnavailable {
+    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
+        match self {
+            Self::InspectFailed => "inspect failed",
+            Self::InspectTimedOut => "inspect timed out",
+            Self::MalformedState => "malformed state",
+            Self::NonTerminal => "container not terminal",
+            Self::DeadlineExpired => "snapshot deadline expired",
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// A typed terminal `.State` (`exited`/`stopped`). `State.Error` is reduced
+/// to whether the runtime reported one; its text is discarded.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub struct ContainerState {
+    pub status: String,
+    /// Raw runtime code; `None` when it is not representable as `i32`.
+    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,
+    pub oom_marker: bool,
+    pub error_reported: bool,
+    pub started_at: String,
+    pub finished_at: String,
+}
+
+impl ContainerState {
+    /// Parse `{{json .State}}`: every required field must have its type; an
+    /// integer code outside `i32` is kept as `None`, a non-integer refuses.
+    pub fn from_inspect_json(json: &[u8]) -> Option<Self> {
+        let state: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(json).ok()?;
+        let text = |key: &str| state.get(key)?.as_str().map(str::to_owned);
+        let code = state.get("ExitCode")?;
+        let exit_code = match (code.as_i64(), code.as_u64()) {
+            (Some(code), _) => i32::try_from(code).ok(),
+            (None, Some(_)) => None,
+            _ => return None,
+        };
+        Some(Self {
+            status: text("Status")?,
+            exit_code,
+            oom_marker: state.get("OOMKilled")?.as_bool()?,
+            error_reported: !text("Error")?.is_empty(),
+            started_at: text("StartedAt")?,
+            finished_at: text("FinishedAt")?,
+        })
+    }
+
+    /// Only `exited`/`stopped` may be decoded as an exit.
+    pub fn is_terminal(&self) -> bool {
+        matches!(self.status.as_str(), "exited" | "stopped")
+    }

+/// A runtime pidfile: ASCII digits plus at most one final newline, `1..=i32::MAX`.
+pub fn parse_pidfile(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<u32> {
+    let digits = bytes.strip_suffix(b"\n").unwrap_or(bytes);
+    if digits.is_empty() || digits.len() > 10 || !digits.iter().all(u8::is_ascii_digit) {
+        return None;
+    }
+    let pid: u64 = std::str::from_utf8(digits).ok()?.parse().ok()?;
+    u32::try_from(pid)
+        .ok()
+        .filter(|pid| (1..=i32::MAX as u32).contains(pid))
+}
+
+/// A CID receipt: exactly 64 lowercase hex plus at most one final newline.
+pub fn parse_container_id(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {
+    let hex = bytes.strip_suffix(b"\n").unwrap_or(bytes);
+    let valid = hex.len() == 64 && hex.iter().all(|b| matches!(b, b'0'..=b'9' | b'a'..=b'f'));
+    valid.then(|| String::from_utf8_lossy(hex).into_owned())
+}

+/// `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` names `cid` in an exact path component (systemd
+/// `libpod-<cid>.scope`, cgroupfs `libpod-<cid>`, split `libpod-payload-<cid>`).
+pub fn cgroup_names_container(cgroup: &str, cid: &str) -> bool {
+    let names = [
+        format!("libpod-{cid}.scope"),
+        format!("libpod-{cid}"),
+        format!("libpod-payload-{cid}"),
+    ];
+    cgroup
+        .lines()
+        .filter_map(|line| line.splitn(3, ':').nth(2))
+        .flat_map(|path| path.split('/'))
+        .any(|part| names.iter().any(|name| name == part))

+/// The one immutable terminal snapshot both classifiers read.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub struct ContainerTerminalFacts {
+    pub state: Result<ContainerState, TerminalUnavailable>,
+    pub payload: PayloadExit,
+    pub source: PayloadExitSource,
+}
+
+impl ContainerTerminalFacts {
+    /// Apply the decoding rule: a verified pidfd status wins; otherwise only an
+    /// unambiguous terminal runtime code (`0..=128`, `193..=255`) decodes.
+    pub fn new(
+        state: Result<ContainerState, TerminalUnavailable>,
+        pidfd: Option<PayloadExit>,
+    ) -> Self {
+        let runtime = state.as_ref().ok().and_then(|s| s.exit_code);
+        let (payload, source) = match (pidfd, runtime) {
+            (Some(exit), _) => (exit, PayloadExitSource::Pidfd),
+            (None, Some(code @ (0..=128 | 193..=255))) => {
+                (PayloadExit::Exited(code as u8), PayloadExitSource::Runtime)
+            }
+            _ => (PayloadExit::Unknown, PayloadExitSource::None),
+        };
+        Self {
+            state,
+            payload,
+            source,
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// §Classification (T3), excluding the `PlannedStop` latch the caller owns.
+    pub fn classify(&self, stderr_tail: Option<String>) -> crate::supervision::CrashCause {
+        use crate::supervision::{CrashCause, FaultCause};
+        let truncated = |why: &str| {
+            CrashCause::Fault(FaultCause::Truncated {
+                reason: format!("container terminal facts: {why}"),
+            })
+        };
+        let state = match &self.state {
+            Ok(state) => state,
+            Err(why) => return truncated(why.as_str()),
+        };
+        let fault = CrashCause::Fault;
+        match (self.payload, state.exit_code) {
+            (PayloadExit::Exited(0), _) => CrashCause::Voluntary,
+            (PayloadExit::Exited(code), _) => fault(FaultCause::NonZeroExit {
+                code: code.into(),
+                stderr_tail,
+            }),
+            (PayloadExit::Signaled(9), _) if state.oom_marker => fault(FaultCause::OomKilled {
+                signal: Some(9),
+                stderr_tail,
+            }),
+            (PayloadExit::Signaled(signal), _) => fault(FaultCause::SignaledByKernel {
+                signal: signal.into(),
+                stderr_tail,
+            }),
+            (PayloadExit::Unknown, Some(137)) if state.oom_marker => fault(FaultCause::OomKilled {
+                signal: None,
+                stderr_tail,
+            }),
+            (PayloadExit::Unknown, Some(code @ 129..=192)) => {
+                fault(FaultCause::NonZeroExit { code, stderr_tail })
+            }
+            (PayloadExit::Unknown, _) => truncated("no valid exit evidence"),
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The verified payload exit code the completion oracle may use.
+    pub fn completion_exit_code(&self) -> Option<i32> {
+        match (&self.state, self.payload) {
+            (Ok(_), PayloadExit::Exited(code)) => Some(code.into()),
+            _ => None,
+        }
+    }
+}

+        let state = facts.state.as_ref().ok();

+                .and_then(|rest| rest.strip_suffix(')'))

+                .filter(|n| !n.starts_with('0') || n.len() == 1)
+                .and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())
+                .filter(|n| (min..=max).contains(n))

+        let signaled = decoded("signaled(sig=", 64, 1);

+            }),

+        source_ok && self.removed == self.residue.is_none()

+use maos_domain::{
+    sandbox::{
+        cgroup_names_container, parse_container_id, parse_pidfile, ContainerExitRecord,
+        ContainerResidue, ContainerState, ContainerTerminalFacts, PayloadExit, PayloadExitSource,
+        TerminalUnavailable,
+    },

+};
+use serde_json::{json, Value};
+
+fn state(code: Option<i32>, oom: bool) -> ContainerState {
+    ContainerState {
+        status: "exited".into(),
+        exit_code: code,
+        oom_marker: oom,
+        error_reported: false,
+        started_at: "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z".into(),
+        finished_at: "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z".into(),
+    }
+}
+fn facts(code: Option<i32>, oom: bool, payload: Option<PayloadExit>) -> ContainerTerminalFacts {
+    ContainerTerminalFacts::new(Ok(state(code, oom)), payload)
+}
+fn fault(cause: CrashCause) -> FaultCause {
+    match cause {
+        CrashCause::Fault(f) => f,
+        CrashCause::Voluntary => panic!("expected fault"),
+        _ => panic!("unrecognized crash cause"),
+    }
+}

+#[test]
+fn unavailable_state_is_always_truncated_even_with_clean_runtime_client() {
+    for reason in [
+        TerminalUnavailable::InspectFailed,
+        TerminalUnavailable::InspectTimedOut,
+        TerminalUnavailable::MalformedState,
+        TerminalUnavailable::NonTerminal,
+        TerminalUnavailable::DeadlineExpired,
+    ] {
+        let f = ContainerTerminalFacts::new(Err(reason), None);
+        assert!(matches!(
+            fault(f.classify(None)),
+            FaultCause::Truncated { .. }
+        ));
+        assert_eq!(f.completion_exit_code(), None);
+    }
+}
+#[test]
+fn payload_classification_obeys_oom_authority_and_fallback() {
+    assert_eq!(
+        facts(Some(0), false, Some(PayloadExit::Exited(0))).classify(None),
+        CrashCause::Voluntary
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        facts(Some(0), true, Some(PayloadExit::Exited(0))).classify(None),
+        CrashCause::Voluntary
+    );
+    assert!(matches!(
+        fault(facts(Some(9), false, Some(PayloadExit::Exited(9))).classify(None)),
+        FaultCause::NonZeroExit { code: 9, .. }
+    ));
+    let oom = facts(Some(137), true, Some(PayloadExit::Signaled(9))).classify(None);
+    assert_eq!(oom.exit_signal(), Some(9));
+    assert_eq!(oom.exit_code(), None);
+    assert_eq!(oom.as_str(), "fault.oom_killed");
+    assert!(matches!(
+        fault(facts(Some(143), false, Some(PayloadExit::Signaled(15))).classify(None)),
+        FaultCause::SignaledByKernel { signal: 15, .. }
+    ));
+    assert!(matches!(
+        fault(facts(Some(137), true, None).classify(None)),
+        FaultCause::OomKilled { signal: None, .. }
+    ));
+    assert!(matches!(
+        fault(facts(Some(129), false, None).classify(None)),
+        FaultCause::NonZeroExit { code: 129, .. }
+    ));
+    assert!(matches!(
+        fault(facts(Some(192), false, None).classify(None)),
+        FaultCause::NonZeroExit { code: 192, .. }
+    ));
+    assert_eq!(
+        facts(Some(0), true, Some(PayloadExit::Exited(0))).classify(None),

+    assert!(matches!(

+        (129, PayloadExit::Unknown, PayloadExitSource::None),

+            Ok(()),
+        ),

+        ContainerExitRecord::new(&facts(Some(0), false, None), Ok(())),
+        ContainerExitRecord::new(&facts(Some(137), false, None), Ok(())),
+        record(
+            None,
+            false,
+            PayloadExit::Unknown,
+            PayloadExitSource::None,
+            Ok(()),
+        ),
+        record(
+            Some(137),
+            true,
+            PayloadExit::Signaled(9),
+            PayloadExitSource::Pidfd,
+            Err(ContainerResidue::StillExists),
+        ),
+    ];
+    for item in cases {
+        assert!(item.is_consistent(), "{item:?}");
+        let value = serde_json::to_value(&item).unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(value.as_object().unwrap().len(), 6);

+#[test]
+fn exit_record_rejects_each_cross_field_inconsistency() {
+    let good = record(
+        Some(0),
+        false,
+        PayloadExit::Exited(0),
+        PayloadExitSource::Pidfd,
+        Ok(()),
+    );
+    let mut bad = good.clone();
+    bad.payload_exit_source = PayloadExitSource::None;
+    assert!(!bad.is_consistent());
+    let mut bad = good.clone();
+    bad.payload_exit_source = PayloadExitSource::Runtime;
+    bad.runtime_exit_code = Some(1);
+    assert!(!bad.is_consistent());
+    let mut bad = good.clone();
+    bad.payload_exit = "garbage".into();
+    assert!(!bad.is_consistent());
+    let mut bad = good.clone();
+    bad.payload_exit = "signaled(sig=0)".into();
+    assert!(!bad.is_consistent());
+    let mut bad = good.clone();
+    bad.payload_exit = "signaled(sig=65)".into();
+    bad.payload_exit_source = PayloadExitSource::Pidfd;
+    assert!(!bad.is_consistent());
+    let mut bad = good.clone();
+    bad.removed = false;
+    assert!(!bad.is_consistent());
+    // 128+N runtime codes are never runtime-decoded payload exits.
+    let mut bad = good.clone();
+    bad.payload_exit = "exited(code=137)".into();
+    bad.payload_exit_source = PayloadExitSource::Runtime;
+    bad.runtime_exit_code = Some(137);
+    assert!(!bad.is_consistent());
+    let mut bad = good.clone();
+    bad.payload_exit = "exited(code=+1)".into();
+    assert!(!bad.is_consistent());
+    let mut bad = good;
+    bad.residue = Some(ContainerResidue::RemoveFailed);
+    assert!(!bad.is_consistent());
+}

+/// Open a pidfd on any process, child or not.
+#[doc(hidden)]
+pub fn pidfd_open(pid: u32) -> io::Result<std::os::fd::OwnedFd> {
+    use std::os::fd::FromRawFd;
+    let pid =
+        libc::pid_t::try_from(pid).map_err(|_| io::Error::from(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput))?;
+    // SAFETY: pidfd_open(2) takes a PID and zero flags by value, reads no
+    // caller memory, and returns a new descriptor or -1.
+    let fd = unsafe { libc::syscall(libc::SYS_pidfd_open, pid, 0) };
+    if fd < 0 {
+        return Err(io::Error::last_os_error());
+    }
+    // SAFETY: a non-negative pidfd_open result is a fresh descriptor that
+    // nothing else in this process owns.
+    Ok(unsafe { std::os::fd::OwnedFd::from_raw_fd(fd as libc::c_int) })
+}

+/// `poll(2)` once; the caller owns `EINTR` retries and deadlines.
+#[doc(hidden)]
+pub fn poll_ready(fds: &mut [libc::pollfd], timeout: std::time::Duration) -> io::Result<usize> {
+    let ms = libc::c_int::try_from(timeout.as_millis()).unwrap_or(libc::c_int::MAX);
+    // SAFETY: `fds` is an exclusively borrowed, initialized array of exactly
+    // `fds.len()` pollfd entries for the duration of the call.
+    let ready = unsafe { libc::poll(fds.as_mut_ptr(), fds.len() as libc::nfds_t, ms) };
+    usize::try_from(ready).map_err(|_| io::Error::last_os_error())
+}

+/// `true` once `fd` polls readable within `timeout` (a pidfd: the process exited).
+#[doc(hidden)]
+pub fn readable(fd: std::os::fd::BorrowedFd<'_>, timeout: std::time::Duration) -> bool {
+    let mut fds = [libc::pollfd {
+        fd: fd.as_raw_fd(),
+        events: libc::POLLIN,
+        revents: 0,
+    }];
+    poll_ready(&mut fds, timeout).is_ok_and(|ready| ready > 0)

+/// The raw wait status, only when the kernel returned the `PIDFD_INFO_EXIT`
+/// bit (Linux >= 6.15); never a zero-initialized field without it.
+#[doc(hidden)]
+pub fn pidfd_exit_status(pidfd: std::os::fd::BorrowedFd<'_>) -> io::Result<Option<i32>> {
+    let exit = u64::from(libc::PIDFD_INFO_EXIT);
+    // SAFETY: `pidfd_info` is plain integers, so all-zero is a valid value;
+    // PIDFD_GET_INFO then reads and writes exactly that one struct through a
+    // valid, exclusively borrowed pointer.
+    let (result, info) = unsafe {
+        let mut info: libc::pidfd_info = std::mem::zeroed();
+        info.mask = exit;

+    }
+    Ok((info.mask & exit != 0).then_some(info.exit_code))
+}

+/// Read a small runtime-written receipt without ever blocking on the path:
+/// hold the inode `O_PATH | O_NOFOLLOW`, require a regular file, reopen the held
+/// inode through procfs non-blocking, re-check its identity, read `<= max` bytes.
+#[doc(hidden)]
+#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
+pub fn read_receipt(path: &Path, max: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
+    read_receipt_after_hold(path, max, || {})
+}
+
+/// Deterministic held-inode seam: `after_hold` runs after `O_PATH` opens the
+/// pathname and before bytes are read from that descriptor.
+#[doc(hidden)]
+#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
+pub fn read_receipt_after_hold(
+    path: &Path,
+    max: usize,
+    after_hold: impl FnOnce(),
+) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
+    use std::io::Read;
+    use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;
+    use std::os::unix::fs::{MetadataExt, OpenOptionsExt};
+    let held = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
+        .read(true)
+        .custom_flags(libc::O_PATH | libc::O_NOFOLLOW | libc::O_CLOEXEC)
+        .open(path)
+        .ok()?;
+    after_hold();
+    let meta = held.metadata().ok()?;
+    if !meta.is_file() {
+        return None;
+    }
+    let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
+        .read(true)
+        .custom_flags(libc::O_NONBLOCK | libc::O_CLOEXEC)
+        .open(format!("/proc/self/fd/{}", held.as_raw_fd()))
+        .ok()?;
+    let again = file.metadata().ok()?;
+    if !again.is_file() || again.dev() != meta.dev() || again.ino() != meta.ino() {
+        return None;
+    }
+    let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(max + 1);
+    file.take(max as u64 + 1).read_to_end(&mut bytes).ok()?;
+    (bytes.len() <= max).then_some(bytes)
+}

+/// The per-spawn state directory must be a fresh, empty, mode-0700 directory
+/// owned by the daemon's effective uid. Checked before any runtime call.
+#[doc(hidden)]
+#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
+pub fn validate_state_dir(dir: &Path) -> Result<(), T3Error> {
+    use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
+    let meta = std::fs::symlink_metadata(dir).map_err(|_| T3Error::StateDir("missing"))?;
+    let euid = std::fs::metadata("/proc/self")
+        .map_err(|_| T3Error::StateDir("effective uid unknown"))?
+        .uid();
+    if !meta.is_dir() {
+        Err(T3Error::StateDir("not a directory"))
+    } else if meta.uid() != euid {
+        Err(T3Error::StateDir("not owned by the daemon's effective uid"))
+    } else if meta.mode() & 0o7777 != 0o700 {
+        Err(T3Error::StateDir("not mode 0700"))
+    } else if std::fs::read_dir(dir).map_or(true, |mut entries| entries.next().is_some()) {
+        Err(T3Error::StateDir("not empty"))
+    } else {
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}

+/// Trust a pidfd on the pidfile PID only if `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` names the CID
+/// in an exact component and the pidfd is still live after that read.
+#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
+fn open_payload_pidfd(pid: u32, cid: &str) -> Option<std::os::fd::OwnedFd> {
+    use crate::security::sandbox::linux;
+    use std::os::fd::AsFd;
+    let pidfd = linux::pidfd_open(pid).ok()?;
+    let cgroup = std::fs::read_to_string(format!("/proc/{pid}/cgroup")).ok()?;
+    let owned = maos_domain::sandbox::cgroup_names_container(&cgroup, cid);
+    (owned && !linux::readable(pidfd.as_fd(), Duration::ZERO)).then_some(pidfd)

+fn signed_test_image() -> VerifiedImageAttestation {
+    use maos_kernel_core::security::crypto::RingCryptoProvider;
+    use ring::signature::{Ed25519KeyPair, KeyPair};
+
+    let seed = [0u8; 32];
+    let keypair = Ed25519KeyPair::from_seed_unchecked(&seed).unwrap();
+    let public: [u8; 32] = keypair.public_key().as_ref().try_into().unwrap();
+    let entries =
+        vec![
+            T3ImageEntry::new("registry.example/maos", [0x11; 32], "stub test image", true)
+                .unwrap(),
+        ];
+    let signature = RingCryptoProvider
+        .sign_capability_token(&seed, &serde_json::to_vec(&entries).unwrap())
+        .unwrap();
+    let attestation = T3ImageAttestation::new(
+        ImageAttestationId([1; 32]),
+        1,
+        1,
+        entries,
+        signature.try_into().unwrap(),
+        public,
+    )
+    .unwrap();
+    let temp = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
+    let lock = temp.path().join("lock.json");
+    fs::write(&lock, serde_json::to_vec(&vec![attestation]).unwrap()).unwrap();
+    load_and_verify_lock_at(&lock, &public, &RingCryptoProvider)
+        .unwrap()
+        .default_entry()
+        .unwrap()

+fn receipts_are_nonblocking_held_regular_files_with_bounded_contents() {

+    let good = temp.path().join("good");

+    assert_eq!(read_receipt(&good, 11), Some(b"123\n".to_vec()));
+    assert_eq!(read_receipt(&temp.path().join("missing"), 11), None);
+    let dangling = temp.path().join("dangling");
+    symlink(temp.path().join("absent"), &dangling).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(read_receipt(&dangling, 11), None);
+    let valid_link = temp.path().join("valid-link");
+    symlink(&good, &valid_link).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(read_receipt(&valid_link, 11), None);
+    let dir = temp.path().join("directory");
+    fs::create_dir(&dir).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(read_receipt(&dir, 11), None);
+    for bytes in [b"123456789012".as_slice(), b"12x", b"abc", b"0"] {
+        let path = temp.path().join("case");
+        fs::write(&path, bytes).unwrap();
+        let result = read_receipt(&path, 11);
+        if bytes.len() > 11 {
+            assert_eq!(result, None);
+        } else {
+            assert_eq!(result, Some(bytes.to_vec()));
+            assert_eq!(maos_domain::sandbox::parse_pidfile(&result.unwrap()), None);
+        }
+    }
+    let fifo = temp.path().join("fifo");
+    let c = CString::new(fifo.as_os_str().as_bytes()).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::mkfifo(c.as_ptr(), 0o600) }, 0);
+    let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
+    std::thread::spawn(move || {
+        let result = read_receipt(&fifo, 11);
+        let _ = tx.send(result);
+    });
+    assert_eq!(
+        rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_millis(500))
+            .expect("FIFO read must not block"),

+    fs::write(&replaced, b"42").unwrap();
+    let bytes = read_receipt_after_hold(&replaced, 11, || {
+        fs::rename(&replaced, &old_inode).unwrap();
+        fs::write(&replaced, b"99").unwrap();
+    });
+    assert_eq!(bytes, Some(b"42".to_vec()));
+    assert_eq!(fs::read(&replaced).unwrap(), b"99");

+fn bounded_invocation_drains_caps_and_enforces_deadlines() {
+    let shell = Path::new("/bin/sh");
+    let filled = invoke_bounded(
+        shell,
+        &[
+            "-c",
+            "head -c 100000 /dev/zero; head -c 100000 /dev/zero >&2",
+        ],
+        &[],
+        Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(3),
+    );
+    match filled {
+        Invocation::Exited {
+            status,
+            stdout,
+            stderr,
+            stdout_complete,
+            stderr_complete,
+        } => {
+            assert!(status.success());
+            assert_eq!(stdout.len(), 64 * 1024);
+            assert_eq!(stderr.len(), 64 * 1024);
+            assert!(!stdout_complete, "truncated stdout is incomplete");
+            assert!(!stderr_complete, "truncated stderr is incomplete");
+        }
+        other => panic!("unexpected invocation: {other:?}"),
+    }
+    let held = Instant::now();
+    let descendant = invoke_bounded(
+        shell,
+        &["-c", "(sleep 3) & exit 0"],
+        &[],
+        held + Duration::from_secs(3),
+    );
+    match descendant {
+        Invocation::Exited {
+            stdout_complete,
+            stderr_complete,
+            ..
+        } => {
+            assert!(!stdout_complete, "descendant-held stdout is incomplete");
+            assert!(!stderr_complete, "descendant-held stderr is incomplete");
+        }
+        other => panic!("unexpected invocation: {other:?}"),
+    }
+    assert!(held.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(2));
+    let delayed = invoke_bounded(
+        shell,
+        &[
+            "-c",
+            "(sleep 0.4; printf 'volume cleanup failed\\n' >&2) & exit 0",
+        ],
+        &[],
+        Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(2),
+    );
+    match delayed {
+        Invocation::Exited {
+            stderr,
+            stderr_complete,
+            ..
+        } => {
+            assert!(!stderr_complete, "200 ms drain grace cannot certify stderr");
+            assert!(!String::from_utf8_lossy(&stderr).contains("volume cleanup failed"));
+        }
+        other => panic!("unexpected invocation: {other:?}"),
+    }
+    let start = Instant::now();
+    assert!(matches!(
+        invoke_bounded(
+            shell,
+            &["-c", "sleep 2"],
+            &[],
+            start + Duration::from_millis(150)

+    assert!(start.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(1));
+    assert!(matches!(

+            Path::new("/definitely/not/a/program"),
+            &[],
+            &[],
+            Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(1)
+        ),

+fn kernel_supports_pidfd_info_exit() -> bool {
+    let output = Command::new("uname").arg("-r").output().unwrap();
+    let version = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);
+    let mut parts = version
+        .split('.')
+        .filter_map(|part| part.split('-').next()?.parse::<u32>().ok());
+    matches!((parts.next(), parts.next()), (Some(major), Some(minor)) if major > 6 || (major == 6 && minor >= 15))
+}
+fn require_pidfd_exit() -> bool {
+    if kernel_supports_pidfd_info_exit() {
+        return true;
+    }
+    let version = Command::new("uname").arg("-r").output().unwrap();
+    let kernel = String::from_utf8_lossy(&version.stdout).trim().to_owned();
+    if std::env::var_os("CI").is_some() {
+        panic!("PIDFD_INFO_EXIT requires Linux >= 6.15; CI kernel is {kernel}");
+    }
+    eprintln!("SKIP t3_terminal_helpers_17_7: kernel {kernel} predates Linux 6.15 PIDFD_INFO_EXIT");
+    false
+}

+    if !require_pidfd_exit() {
+        return;
+    }
+    use std::os::fd::AsFd;
+    // Evidence may lag readability until the reaper runs: poll like production.
+    let exit_status = |fd: &std::os::fd::OwnedFd| {
+        let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5);
+        loop {
+            if let Some(raw) = linux::pidfd_exit_status(fd.as_fd()).unwrap() {
+                return Some(raw);
+            }
+            if std::time::Instant::now() >= deadline {
+                return None;
+            }
+            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));
+        }
+    };
+    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
+    let release = dir.path().join("release");
+    // A grandchild (never our child) held until its pidfd is open.
+    let (mut owner, pid) = external_child(&format!(
+        "(while [ ! -e '{}' ]; do sleep 0.01; done; exit 137) & echo $!; wait",
+        release.display()
+    ));
+    let fd = linux::pidfd_open(pid).unwrap();
+    std::fs::write(&release, b"").unwrap();
+    assert!(linux::readable(fd.as_fd(), Duration::from_secs(5)));
+    assert_eq!(exit_status(&fd), Some(0x8900), "exit(137) is Exited(137)");
+    let _ = owner.wait();
+    let (mut owner, pid) = external_child("sleep 30 & echo $!; wait");
+    let fd = linux::pidfd_open(pid).unwrap();
+    Command::new("kill")
+        .args(["-KILL", &pid.to_string()])
+        .status()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert!(linux::readable(fd.as_fd(), Duration::from_secs(5)));
+    assert_eq!(
+        exit_status(&fd),
+        Some(9),
+        "an external SIGKILL is Signaled(9)"
+    );
+    let _ = owner.wait();
+    let mut live = Command::new("sleep").arg("30").spawn().unwrap();
+    let fd = linux::pidfd_open(live.id()).unwrap();
+    assert!(!linux::readable(fd.as_fd(), Duration::from_millis(20)));
+    assert_eq!(linux::pidfd_exit_status(fd.as_fd()).unwrap(), None);
+    live.kill().unwrap();
+    let _ = live.wait();
+}

-On death, MAOS journals `cli.subprocess.exit`, `unplanned_crash`, `lifecycle.crash`, `task.orphaned`, and `worker.completion-verdict`. `[on_crash] action` selects the in-flight task disposition: `nack` (default), `reassign-to-replica`, or `escalate-to-operator`. Under T3, SIGKILL is reported as `exited(code=137)` with `fault.non-zero-exit`; OOM is not distinguished from another SIGKILL. Authoritative container OOM and signal facts are follow-up work. A short-lived Worker that exits before MAOS finishes container PID inspection (about 2.25 s) is refused as a failed launch.
+T3 startup is runtime-owned: MAOS runs `create` → `init`, reads the runtime-written pidfile, then supervises `start --attach`. Containers are not auto-removed (`--rm` is not used) and use `--restart=no`. After terminal facts are read once while the owned CID is retained, teardown performs bounded `rm --force --volumes` and confirms absence with `container exists` for that CID. Short tasks complete without a startup hold. On Linux ≥6.15, payload pidfd `PIDFD_INFO_EXIT` distinguishes an intentional `exit(137)`, external SIGKILL (`fault.signaled`), and OOM (`fault.oom_killed`); when authoritative payload facts are unavailable, documented runtime-evidence fallback rows apply. Exit rows include typed container residue when cleanup cannot be confirmed. Worker unload performs a post-unload registry stop, and its lease ends only after termination is confirmed.
 
 **Resource ceilings:** Manifest and operator limits resolve independently to the stricter value for CPU percentage, memory MiB, PID/task count, and file descriptors. Worker defaults when omitted are `--cpus=1`, `--memory=256m`, and `--pids-limit=64`; omission does not add a manifest ceiling. `cpu_max_pct = 10` maps to `--cpus=0.10`, and `100` to `--cpus=1.00`. `pids_max` independently controls `--pids-limit`; `fd_max` adds explicit equal soft/hard `--ulimit=nofile` limits, never a PID alias. If the requested FD ceiling exceeds the inherited hard ceiling, launch refuses rather than clamps. This T3 route is Linux x64 only; supported native runtime proof covers Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 x64 and arm images, while T3 is x64 only. No macOS/Windows resource equivalence is claimed.
 
 For native Linux T2, MAOS requires a writable delegated cgroup v2 domain for explicit CPU or PID caps and refuses before guest code if unavailable. A memory-only request may instead retain `RLIMIT_AS` (and optional `RLIMIT_NOFILE`) and emit one persisted `ResourceCeilingDowngraded=20` informational lifecycle row on each successful fallback launch; FD-only and no-resource launches do not emit it. This is not a state transition. The native journal adapter appends after live Worker ownership/observer registration and before startup publication; append failure still panics and `sync_data` errors remain ignored, so no power-loss durability guarantee is added. Run local native cgroup smoke coverage through `python3 scripts/run_cgroup_ceiling_17_2.py run --mode delegated|undelegated --unit maos-17-2-NAME --timeout SECONDS -- COMMAND` (add `--rootless-canary` for the same-UID rootless canary).

+Root shutdown takes custody before container creation, joins in-flight initialization before removal, and prevents a cancelled launch from starting afterward. Exit observation, explicit stop, bridge finalization, and guard cleanup share the original absolute teardown deadline. Truncated runtime diagnostics or a pipe left open by a runtime descendant cannot certify volume cleanup, even when `rm` exits successfully; they retain typed residue. A failed CID kill is reported independently of later successful removal. When `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is unavailable, temporary custody directories are scoped by effective UID so one user cannot block another user's launch. OOM attribution also requires the runtime's OOM marker; pidfd evidence alone proves the signal, not its cause.

@@ -0,0 +1,215 @@
+//! Story 17-7 — pin the T3 terminal-facts workflow route and aggregate gate.
+use serde_yaml::Value;
+use std::{collections::BTreeMap, fs, path::PathBuf};
+
+fn workflow() -> Value {
+    let path =
+        PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../.github/workflows/discipline.yml");
+    serde_yaml::from_str(&fs::read_to_string(path).expect("discipline workflow"))
+        .expect("workflow YAML")
+}
+fn get<'a>(value: &'a Value, name: &str) -> &'a Value {
+    value
+        .as_mapping()
+        .expect("mapping")
+        .get(&Value::String(name.into()))
+        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("missing {name}"))
+}
+fn steps(job: &Value) -> &[Value] {
+    get(job, "steps").as_sequence().expect("steps")
+}
+fn named<'a>(job: &'a Value, name: &str) -> &'a Value {
+    steps(job)
+        .iter()
+        .find(|step| step["name"].as_str() == Some(name))
+        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("missing step {name}"))
+}
+// Remove only the new required-job predicate from a scratch workflow copy.
+fn workflow_with_predicate(predicate: bool) -> Value {
+    let mut value = workflow();
+    if !predicate {
+        for step in value["jobs"]["aggregate"]["steps"]
+            .as_sequence_mut()
+            .expect("aggregate steps")
+        {
+            if step["name"].as_str() == Some("Check for failures") {
+                let script = step["run"]
+                    .as_str()
+                    .expect("status script")
+                    .replace(" || needs['epic-17-exit'].result != 'success'", "");
+                step["run"] = Value::String(script);
+            }
+            if step["name"].as_str() == Some("Fail if any gate failed") {
+                let predicate = " || needs['epic-17-exit'].result != 'success'";
+                let condition = step["if"].as_str().expect("failure predicate");
+                step["if"] = Value::String(condition.replace(predicate, ""));
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    value
+}
+
+fn dependencies(aggregate: &Value) -> BTreeMap<String, String> {
+    get(aggregate, "needs")
+        .as_sequence()
+        .expect("aggregate needs")
+        .iter()
+        .map(|name| {
+            (
+                name.as_str().expect("job name").to_owned(),
+                "success".to_owned(),
+            )
+        })
+        .collect()
+}
+
+fn evaluate(expr: &str, needs: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> bool {
+    let e = expr
+        .trim()
+        .trim_start_matches("${{")
+        .trim_end_matches("}}")
+        .trim();
+    e.split("||").any(|term| {
+        let term = term.trim().trim_matches(|c| c == '(' || c == ')').trim();
+        if term.starts_with("contains(needs.*.result,") {
+            let state = term.split('\'').nth(1).expect("contains state");
+            return needs.values().any(|value| value == state);
+        }
+        let start = term.find("needs['").expect("needs bracket result") + 7;
+        let end = term[start..].find("']").expect("needs closing bracket") + start;
+        let name = &term[start..end];
+        let state = needs.get(name).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("");
+        assert_eq!(
+            term[end + 2..].trim(),
+            ".result != 'success'",
+            "unsupported required-job predicate: {term}"
+        );
+        state != "success"
+    })
+}
+
+fn render_run(script: &str, needs: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> String {
+    let start = script.find("${{").expect("GHA expression in status script");
+    let end = script[start..].find("}}").expect("expression end") + start + 2;
+    script.replacen(
+        &script[start..end],
+        if evaluate(&script[start..end], needs) {
+            "true"
+        } else {
+            "false"
+        },
+        1,
+    )
+}
+
+fn fresh_dir(prefix: &str) -> PathBuf {
+    let nonce = std::time::SystemTime::now()
+        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
+        .expect("clock")
+        .as_nanos();
+    let path = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("{prefix}-{}-{nonce}", std::process::id()));
+    fs::create_dir(&path).expect("fresh temp dir");
+    path
+}
+
+fn output(script: &str) -> String {
+    let dir = fresh_dir("maos-terminal-workflow");
+    let file = dir.join("output");
+    let status = std::process::Command::new("bash")
+        .arg("-e")
+        .arg("-c")
+        .arg(script)
+        .env("GITHUB_OUTPUT", &file)
+        .status()
+        .expect("bash status script");
+    let value = fs::read_to_string(&file).expect("GITHUB_OUTPUT");
+    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(dir);
+    assert!(status.success(), "aggregate status shell failed");
+    value
+}
+
+fn run_successful(script: &str) -> bool {
+    let dir = fresh_dir("maos-terminal-failure");
+    let status = std::process::Command::new("bash")
+        .arg("-e")
+        .arg("-c")
+        .arg(script)
+        .env("GITHUB_OUTPUT", dir.join("output"))
+        .status()
+        .expect("failure step shell");
+    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(dir);
+    status.success()
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn aggregate_workflow_executes_non_success_handling_and_failure_step() {
+    let value = workflow();
+    let aggregate = &value["jobs"]["aggregate"];
+    assert!(
+        get(aggregate, "needs")
+            .as_sequence()
+            .expect("aggregate needs")
+            .iter()
+            .any(|dependency| dependency.as_str() == Some("epic-17-exit")),
+        "epic-17-exit must be a required aggregate dependency"
+    );
+    let dependencies = dependencies(aggregate);
+    let script = named(aggregate, "Check for failures")["run"]
+        .as_str()
+        .expect("status script");
+    let failure = named(aggregate, "Fail if any gate failed");
+    let failure_if = failure["if"].as_str().expect("failure predicate");
+    let failure_run = failure["run"].as_str().expect("failure shell");
+
+    for state in ["skipped", "failure", "cancelled"] {
+        let job = "epic-17-exit";
+        let mut needs = dependencies.clone();
+        needs.insert(job.to_owned(), state.to_owned());
+        assert_eq!(
+            output(&render_run(script, &needs)).trim(),
+            "overall=failure",
+            "{job}={state}"
+        );
+        assert!(
+            evaluate(failure_if, &needs),
+            "failure step must run for {job}={state}"
+        );
+        assert!(
+            !run_successful(failure_run),
+            "failure step must exit nonzero for {job}={state}"
+        );
+    }
+
+    assert_eq!(
+        output(&render_run(script, &dependencies)).trim(),
+        "overall=success"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        !evaluate(failure_if, &dependencies),
+        "failure step selected all-success control"
+    );
+
+    // Removing the target predicate makes the status condition false for a
+    // skipped dependency. Its shell would not run, leaving the default
+    // successful output; the failure-step condition must catch this case.
+    let without = workflow_with_predicate(false);
+    let omitted = &without["jobs"]["aggregate"];
+    let omitted_script = named(omitted, "Check for failures")["run"]
+        .as_str()
+        .expect("status script without target predicate");
+    let mut needs = dependencies.clone();
+    needs.insert("epic-17-exit".into(), "skipped".into());
+    assert_eq!(
+        output(&render_run(omitted_script, &needs)).trim(),
+        "overall=success"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        !evaluate(
+            named(omitted, "Fail if any gate failed")["if"]
+                .as_str()
+                .expect("failure predicate"),
+            &needs
+        ),
+        "predicate removal must expose skipped job as missed failure"
+    );
+}
